writeSwitch.label: Allow MCP writes
writeSwitch.hint: With the switch on, read and write tokens can create tickets, change status and priority, edit title and description, move tickets in the tree, change dependencies, comment and mark work in progress, with the permissions of each token's person. With it off, no token writes, whatever its scope.

scope.label: Scope
scope.readHint: The AI client can only read the project's tickets.
scope.writeHint: Besides reading, the AI client will be able to create tickets, change status and priority, edit title and description, move tickets in the tree, change dependencies, comment and mark work in progress, with the permissions of your own account.
scope.writeOff: MCP writes are off for the organization: this token will only write once an administrator turns the switch on.

mcp.tokensOff: MCP access is off. Turn it on in AI clients (MCP) to create tokens.
mcp.connectHint: Create a token in Your tokens: the command to connect the client appears right after you create it.

state.writeOn: MCP access is on; writing is on.
state.writeOff: MCP access is on; writing is off.

peopleSwitch.label: People and conversations
peopleSwitch.hint: With the switch on, the AI clients of anyone holding a token with this scope receive the names of people, assignees, comments, the history of tickets and the conversations of the project the person takes part in, including messages from other people. TreePM does not control what the client and its provider do with it. It needs MCP access to be on.

people.label: People and conversations
people.hint: The AI client will receive the names of people, assignees, comments, the history of tickets and the conversations of the project you take part in, including messages from other people, and can set assignees if the token can also write. It applies on every call, as long as the organization switch stays on.
people.off: The people and conversations scope is off for the organization: an administrator has to turn it on before you can create a token with it.

ai.title: AI and privacy
ai.outdated: The documents changed (version {{current}}) and the earlier acceptance no longer applies. It must be accepted again.
ai.failed: The acceptance could not be changed. Try again.
ai.versionChanged: The documents changed while you were reading. Read the current version and accept again.

assistant.heading: AI assistant
assistant.explain: By accepting, the text of tickets and of conversations with the assistant is sent to Anthropic and TypeSafe for the AI features, and the title and description of tickets also go to Voyage AI, which generates the vectors for search by meaning. Names, emails and identifiers of people are not sent.
assistant.accept: Accept and turn on the assistant
assistant.withdrawWarning: The assistant stops working in the organization: the new-ticket conversation, finding the place, group texts, writing in the description and questions about the project. AI code reading is withdrawn too.

codeReading.heading: AI code reading
codeReading.explain: By accepting, snippets of code from the linked repositories will be sent to Anthropic, and only to it. This feature is not available yet; the acceptance can already be given.
codeReading.withdrawWarning: The AI can no longer read code from the linked repositories.

language.lead: The language of the interface menus, buttons and notices.

linear.lead: Bring the issues of a Linear team into a project. The key is yours: it is stored encrypted, only you use it, and TreePM only reads, it never writes to Linear.

people.title: People
people.lead: Who is part of the organization. Test people exist only to try out conversations: they cannot sign in on their own, and only an administrator can view the app as them.

linear.title: Linear
linear.actingAs: The Linear key is personal and cannot be used as another person. Go back to being yourself to connect yours.

key.title: Your key
key.label: Personal Linear key
key.guide: In Linear: Settings → Security & access → Personal API keys. Create a read-only key: TreePM never writes to Linear.
key.after: When you connect, TreePM checks the key and shows the workspace and the teams it can see.
key.replaceGuide: Paste the new key. The current one is only replaced if Linear accepts the new one.
key.removeWarning: Removing the key does not undo any project link.
key.footnote: Removing or replacing the key does not undo any link. To import into a linked project, the key must be from the same workspace and see the team.
